svg.title: Blackbody radiation curves
svg.desc: EM radiation intensity versus wavelength for a blackbody at 6000 K (white hot), 4000 K and 3000 K (red hot), drawn to scale from Planck’s law. The 6000 K curve peaks near 480 nm, inside the visible range; cooler bodies radiate far less, and their peaks move to longer wavelengths: about 720 nm at 4000 K and 970 nm, in the infrared, at 3000 K. Ultraviolet lies to the left of the visible band and infrared to the right. An animated companion below illustrates the process; its complete static alternative is shown for reduced motion and print.

g.text: A hotter blackbody peaks at a shorter wavelength
Planck spectrum on one fixed vertical scale. Wien’s law sets λ peak T; total power over all
wavelengths follows T⁴. The total-power ratio is not a truncated-plot integral.
